questions.question: What term is used to describe the random motion of tiny particles suspended in a medium?
options: Osmosis
Brownian motion
Diffusion
Filtration

questions.question: If a substance has particles that are free to move, what will eventually happen to those particles over time?
options: They will clump together at the center.
They will sink to the bottom permanently.
They will reach a random distribution throughout.
They will immediately evaporate into a gas.

questions.question: What is the effect of higher temperatures on the particles in a gas or solution?
options: They move more quickly.
They move more slowly.
They stop moving entirely.
They increase in size.

questions.question: Why are suspensions not classified as solutions?
options: Solid particles cannot be seen at all.
Solid particles can be seen and will eventually settle over time.
Suspensions are always pure substances.
The solid and liquid cannot be separated by filtering.

questions.question: What must happen to the forces of attraction between solute particles for a substance to dissolve?
options: They must be strengthened.
They must remain unchanged.
They have to be overcome.
They must be converted into chemical bonds.

questions.question: When mixing two different liquids, why might the total volume of the mixture be less than the sum of the individual volumes?
options: Particles of one type fit into the spaces between the other type.
Some of the mass is converted into energy.
The particles react to form larger, heavier atoms.
Liquid particles completely shrink when mixed.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes dissolving and melting?
options: Dissolving is a chemical change, while melting is a physical change.
Both are physical processes, but they are not the same thing.
Dissolving and melting are two words for the exact same process.
Melting requires a solvent, while dissolving does not.

questions.question: How is a solution formed?
options: When a soluble solid dissolves in an appropriate solvent
When an insoluble solid is suspended in water
When a liquid is cooled down to its freezing point
When two immiscible liquids are shaken together

questions.question: If you mix 10 g of sugar with 150 g of water, what is the total mass of the mixture?
Which equipment and unit are correctly matched for measuring volume in a laboratory?
options: A balance, in grams
A measuring cylinder, in cm³
A thermometer, in degrees Celsius
A ruler, in centimeters

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of a pure material regarding its physical properties?
options: It has a variable boiling point.
It has a fixed melting point and boiling point.
It melts over a wide range of temperatures.
It does not have a measurable melting point.

questions.question: How do impurities affect the melting and boiling points of a material?
options: They keep the melting and boiling points completely fixed.
They change the melting and boiling point of the material.
They have no effect on either physical property.
They prevent the material from ever changing state.

questions.question: What temperature characteristic is observed when mixtures melt or boil?
options: They melt or boil at a single, sharp temperature.
They melt or boil over a range of temperatures.
They do not have any melting or boiling points.
They only change state at absolute zero.

questions.question: At a given temperature, what limit exists when dissolving a solute in a solvent?
options: There is a limit to how much solute can dissolve.
There is no limit to how much solute can dissolve.
Only exactly one gram of solute can ever dissolve.
Solutes can only dissolve if the mixture is boiled.

questions.question: What can happen to dissolved solutes as a warm solution cools down?
options: They may become insoluble and form crystals.
They will dissolve even more rapidly.
They will evaporate out of the container.
They will turn into a completely new liquid.

questions.question: Upon what factors could the solubility of a substance depend?
options: The size of the solute pieces, choice of solvent, or temperature.
The shape of the beaker and the volume of the room.
The color of the solute and the mass of the stirring rod.
The air pressure and the humidity of the laboratory.

questions.question: In a scientific investigation, what is the independent variable?
options: The variable that is kept the same to make it fair.
The variable that is measured or observed.
The variable that is changed by the investigator.
The equipment used to take measurements.

questions.question: What is the dependent variable in an investigation?
options: The factor that is kept constant throughout.
The factor that is changed on purpose.
The factor that is observed or measured.
The method written to repeat the experiment.
